description:
Fleet defaults for repos that have flipped to GitHub-canonical. Parallel to renovate/default.json, which stays in place for repos still on GitLab CI -- both have to coexist until the migration finishes. Anything platform-neutral is deliberately identical between the two; every difference below is a GitLab coupling that does not survive the move.

Two things from the GitLab preset are absent rather than changed, and neither absence is visible in the rules below. hostRules capping github.com to concurrentRequestLimit 2 is gone: it existed only to stop the terraform manager's provider fan-out (oracle/oci ships 13 platform zips at ~65MiB each) OOMKilling a 1500Mi build container on the self-hosted runner. A hosted runner has 16GB, so the cap now only costs wall-clock. The packageRule disabling the gitlabci-include manager is gone because that manager is never enabled here.

gitAuthor is pinned rather than left to Renovate's default, and gitIgnoredAuthors lists every identity that legitimately commits to a Renovate branch. Both exist because Renovate refuses to rebase a branch carrying a commit from an author it does not recognise -- the branch is treated as human-edited and wedges at need_rebase, with the recompute that would fix it gated off behind the same guard.

Two identities do that here. bump-version commits as github-actions[bot] (hardcoded git config user.email). And since allow_update_branch was turned on fleet-wide, GitHub itself writes 'Merge branch main into renovate/...' commits attributed to the REPOSITORY OWNER, not to the account that enabled auto-merge -- so me@tyler-north.com lands on Renovate branches without anyone typing anything. That second one was missing and was a latent wedge on every open Renovate PR.

The third entry is transitional. Renovate authenticates as the tnoff-ci App now and commits as 324268446+tnoff-ci[bot]@users.noreply.github.com, but every branch it opened before that cutover is authored renovate@whitesourcesoftware.com -- foreign to the new identity, so without this those branches wedge at need_rebase and have to be closed by hand. Removable once no pre-cutover Renovate branch is open.

Note gitAuthor canNOT be pinned from here: it is a self-hosted/global option and Renovate silently ignores it in repository config, which is what a preset is. An earlier attempt to set it here had no effect -- the commits above prove it. If the token identity ever changes again, the fix is another gitIgnoredAuthors entry, or RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR in renovate.yml.

packageRules.description: Automerge the shared reusable-workflow pin. Every consumer SHA-pins tnoff/github-workflows in `uses:`, so one commit there fans out into one PR per repo -- 123 of the 400 dependency MRs merged fleet-wide in the 8 weeks to 2026-08-14 were exactly this, every one hand-merged. The change was already reviewed when it landed on main there; re-approving the same SHA per repo is duplicate review. The consumer's own checks still have to go green first. Matched by package name across BOTH managers rather than by matchManagers: the built-in github-actions manager extracts these pins but never offers an update on them (see the custom manager below), so keying automerge to that manager gated nothing. Both spellings of the name are listed because the two managers name the same dependency differently.

Batch the cloud SDKs. Unchanged from the GitLab preset -- oci, boto3, awscli and friends cut releases most weekdays, so each arrives as its own PR on every run. One grouped PR plus a 7-day floor collapses the intermediate point releases. No additionalBranchPrefix on purpose: each repo's own config decides whether these land under dev- and therefore whether they cut a release.

customManagers.description: terraform-modules is still GitLab-hosted and still SHA-pinned in .tf files, so this carries over unchanged. The .gitlab-ci.yml include-ref manager from the GitLab preset is deliberately absent: the built-in github-actions manager already tracks `uses: ...@<sha>`.

Track tnoff/github-workflows reusable-workflow pins. The built-in github-actions manager only updates a SHA-pinned `uses:` when it carries a `# vX.Y.Z` comment telling it the current version; consumers pin this repo as a bare 40-char SHA, so it extracts the dep and then offers no update -- no error, no warning. Measured 2026-08-28 in one file on public-transit: `actions/checkout@<sha>  # v7.0.1` was bumped twice the same day while the four bare-SHA github-workflows pins beside it never moved, across two dispatched runs and a freshly cut tag. The note on the first packageRule below -- that the built-in manager handles this on GitHub, so the GitLab preset's git-refs manager was not needed -- was wrong, and this restores its equivalent. Same shape as the terraform-modules manager above.
